repos.title: Watched repos
repos.description: owner/name, one per line. This is the watchlist and it lives here, in the task input, the way the Trustpilot actor's categories do. Pick repos only a company running the thing in production would file on.

lookbackDays.title: Lookback days
lookbackDays.description: How far back to read on a first run. After that the actor's own cursor per repo takes over and only genuinely new filings are read.

events.title: Event types
events.description: issue, pr, or both. The GitHub endpoint returns pull requests alongside issues, so this is our filter.

excludeOrgs.title: Extra vendor orgs to exclude
excludeOrgs.description: Every watched repo's owner is excluded automatically. Add anything else whose staff should never count as a prospect, e.g. a vendor that maintains a repo it does not own.

maxPagesPerRepo.title: Max pages per repo
maxPagesPerRepo.description: 100 filings a page. The run stops early anyway once it reaches filings older than the cursor.

maxCompanies.title: Max companies per run
maxCompanies.description: Hard cap on the dataset, so a bad watchlist can never flood the door.

userCacheDays.title: Filer cache days
userCacheDays.description: A filer's employer is looked up once and remembered this long, so a daily run spends almost no requests on people it already knows.

bodyMaxChars.title: Issue body cap
bodyMaxChars.description: The body is the copy ammunition, but Airtable long text dies at 100,000 characters. Keep it well under.

githubToken.title: GitHub token
githubToken.description: A read-only PAT on a dedicated machine account, never the account that owns the Rootworks repo. Falls back to the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable. Without one the run is capped at 60 requests an hour.
